sections.title: Tree and habitat
sections.text: White willow is a fast-growing deciduous tree of wet ground and riverbanks. It commonly reaches 20–30 m tall, with a trunk that may approach 1 m in diameter. Its bark becomes deeply fissured with age.

sections.title: Leaves and catkins
sections.text: Its lance-shaped leaves, about 5–10 cm long, have silky white undersides that give the tree a silvery appearance. The flowers are grouped in catkins; the capsules release tiny, downy seeds. The plate shows the pale foliage and catkins.

sections.title: Uses and caution
sections.text: The bark contains salicin and has been used as a source of salicylate compounds; the wood and flexible twigs have other uses. Willow bark preparations can cause digestive symptoms or allergic reactions; increased bleeding risk is noted for some people, and caution is warranted with salicylate medicines.
